title: Hawley, Murphy Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Hold AI Agents Liable for Hacking
key_facts: Sens. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) announced the AI Agent Accountability Act.
It would apply the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act to operators who knowingly run an AI agent that recklessly causes hacking damage or loss.
Developers would be criminally and civilly liable if they fail to implement reasonable safeguards when they knew or had reason to know of an agent's hacking capabilities.
The attorney general and state attorneys general could sue to block operators and developers who commit or attempt a hacking offence.
Hawley previewed the bill in a Washington Post op-ed and at a 30 Sep Senate Homeland Security committee hearing.
President Trump has repeatedly rejected proposals for additional AI regulation.
quote_evidence: The AI Agent Accountability Act would apply provisions of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act to AI agent operators that knowingly run an AI agent that recklessly causes computer hacking damage or loss.
President Donald Trump has repeatedly rejected proposals for additional AI regulation, arguing that new restrictions could hinder U.S. technological development.
why_it_matters_hint: Would put legal responsibility for AI-agent hacking on the people who build and run the agents.
notes: One outlet; the text describes a proposal, not a law.
